newsitem.title: USA: Morgan's Pelosky sees Telmex sharply up.
newsitem.headline: Morgan's Pelosky sees Telmex sharply up.

text.p: Shares in Telefonos de Mexico SA could rise sharply in 1997, even as the company begins to face competition, the head of Morgan Stanley's Latin American equities said on Monday.

Jay Pelosky, the unit's head, told Reuters that Telmex's shares could trade in the mid-40s this year. The company's American Depositary Receipts (ADR) rose two to 35-3/8 on heavy volume in New York, after it won government approval for a 21 percent rise in local rates.
Pelosky said the rise was helped by portfolio managers who bought shares as a way to get exposure in Mexico, a breach in the stock's resistance level at $34, and such fundamentals as the rate rise.
"The way to play Mexico in 1996 was to long Mexico and stay out of Telmex. In 1997, we do not think that is going to be the case," he said.
Telmex lost its monopoly status on January 1, but Pelosky said the company would be able to weather the competition. He predicted Telmex would only lose 15 percent of its market share this year.
"We think Telmex will surprise," he said. "In other words, we think the market is over-penalizing the competitive threat."
Pelosky said Telmex and Latin American stocks in general would be helped by greater attention from U.S. investors this year as the New York markets lose their luster.

Morgan Stanley's Capital International Index, which monitors the performances of international stocks, shows that Latin America equities typically gain 11.8 percent over the months of December and January, in part because of portfolio rebalancing at year's end.
However, the stocks only gained 3.4 percent from the start of December through Jan 3. That lag means Latin American stocks could see sharp gains this month, Pelosky said.
Morgan Stanley analyst Luiz Carvalho on Monday raised his 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates for Telmex. CS First Boston also raised its rating for Telmex to buy from hold.
